JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 20.03.2024 at about 02-20 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding in a two wheeler bearing reg No. KA-06-HT-4470 as a pillion rider which was ridden by his friend Manjunath from Shambhegowdanapalya village side towards Kunigal side and when they reached near Watch factory, Shabhegowdanapalya-Kunigal road,
Industrial area, Anchepalya Village, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur Dist, at that time the rider of the said Two wheeler had ridden his motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle result of which the vehicle capsized, further result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately,
the petitioner was shifted to CHC Kunigal wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to People Tree Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein admitted as an inpatient for a period of 3 days.
During the hospitalization petitioner was looked after by 2-3 attendants, he spent more than Rs.800/- per day for attendant's charges.

So far, the petitioner has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges etc.,
3.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was doing labour work and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability, the petitioner has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability & loss of income.

4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 /the R.C. owner of two wheeler bearing reg No.
KA- 06-HT-4470 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.

5. Respondent No.2 /the Insurer of two wheeler bearing reg No. KA-06-HT-4470 has filed written statement and contended that there is delay of 16 days in filing the complaint and that the insured vehicle was not involved in the accident, that the petitioner, in collusion with the jurisdictional police and the owner of the vehicle has fixed the vehicle for unlawful gain.
It is further contended that the rider of the insured vehicle was not holding valid driving license and that the petitioner himself by riding the motorcycle has caused for the accident.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES

Gangadhara C M vs Manjunatha on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158902405/
2
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 20-03-2024 at about 2-20 pm., near watch factory,
Shambhegowdanapalya Kunigal road, Industrial area, Anchepalya village, Kunigal Taluk, Tumakur District, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HT-4470?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What order or Award ?
7.
The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and examined one witness as P.W.2 and marked Ex.P1 to ExP12.

On the other hand, Roshan H.S, Specilist Govt, Hospital, Kunigal is examined as RW.2 and got marked document as Ex.R1.
8.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 : - In order to explain the actionable negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, , the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 20.03.2024 at about 02-20 p.m. when the petitioner was proceeding in a two wheeler bearing reg No. KA-06-HT-4470 (herein after called as the offending vehicle) as a pillion rider which was ridden by his friend Manjunath from Shambhegowdanapalya village side towards Kunigal side and when they reached near Watch factory, Shabhegowdanapalya-Kunigal road, Industrial area, Anchepalya Village, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur Dist,

at that time the rider of the said Two wheeler had ridden his motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle result of which the vehicle capsized, further result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle, P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 which are the police records such as FIR with complaint, spot mahazar,
seizure mahazar, sketch, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet.

12. On the basis of the complaint lodged by Rekha.K, case has been registered against the rider of bike in Crime No.0144/2024 of Kunigal PS Traffic Police Station, for the offence punishable under Gangadhara C M vs Manjunatha on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158902405/
3 section 279 and 337 of IPC.

The investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 IPC and under Section 134(a&b) and 187 of MV Act.

13. The Learned counsel for respondent no.2 much argued about the delay in lodging the complaint and submitted that at the time of accident the petitioner himself was riding the motorcycle and he was not traveling in the offending vehicle as pillion rider and in collusion with the police and owner of the offending vehicle, in order to get compensation by projecting him as the pillion rider of the offending vehicle has lodged compliant after 16 days of the accident and
the petitioner being the tortfeasor is not entitled for compensation.

14. In the light of the contention taken by the respondent no.2, if the case paper is perused, it is true that the accident in question has occurred on 20-03-2024 and complaint came to be lodged on 06-04-2024 and there is delay of 16 days in lodging the complaint.

In the complaint and in the FIR reason for delay has been explained stating that the owner of the offending vehicle assured of meeting the medical expenses but later on not come forward to meet the medical expenses hence lodged complaint at belated stage.
The respondent no.2 has produced MLC register as per Ex.R1.
If Ex.R1 is perused, on the date of accident itself the petitioner has taken treatment at Government Hospital Kunigal.
In the Ex.R1 the history of accident is mentioned as "RTA on 20-03- 2024 at about 2-20 pm., skid and fall from bike as pillion rider in KA-06-HT-4470".

From the very document produced by the respondent no.2 clearly proves that the petitioner has met with an accident while he was traveling in the offending vehicle as pillion rider on 20-03-2024 at about 2-20 pm., Hence, there is no reason to accept the version taken by the respondent no.2 stating that the petitioner himself was riding the motorcycle.
Hence, the reason assigned for delay in lodging the complaint appears to be genuine.

15. When it is proved that the petitioner was pillion rider and when the petitioner has categorically stated that due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, this mishap has occurred,
the court has to accept the evidence of PW.1 in the absence of rebuttal evidence from the side of the respondents.

As no other vehicle was involved in the accident and due to the capsize of the offending vehicle, this accident has occurred it can be said without any hesitation that rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
Hence, without discussing much on this point this court holds issue no.1 in the affirmative.
` 16. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summary which are at Ex.P6 and Ex.P9.

On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken primary treatment at Government Hospital on 20-03-2024 and then he was shifted to People Tree Hospitals from 20.03.2024 to 22.03.2024 wherein admitted as an inpatient for a period of 3 days.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained two injuries of which injury no.1 is simple in nature and injury no. 2 is grievous in nature.
17. Dr. Ramesh.B - Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital is examined as PW.2 and through him one OPD book and X-ray are marked as Ex.P11 and 12.

PW.2 has deposed that he examined the Gangadhara C M vs Manjunatha on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158902405/
4 petitioner on 06.10.2024 for assessment of disability and that the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability on the left upper limb at 19% and on the whole body at 7%.
PW.2 further deposed that the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of the implant.
18. If the cross examination of PW.2 is perused, the PW.2 has not given treatment to the petitioner.
Further the fracture is united.
The PW.2 though has stated that petitioner require further treatment for removal of implant but has not stated the approximate cost of the surgery.
The PW.2 has assessed the disability of the petitioner on left upper limb at 19% and to the whole body at 7%.
As per the very evidence of PW.2, the petitioner has left clavicle fracture.
No disability arises for the fracture of clavicle bone.
Hence, this court declines to consider the disability assessed by the PW.2.
Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injury it may have caused some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.

Hence, instead of awarding compensation under the head loss of future income, this court would award compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort to the tune of Rs.1,25,000/-.
19.
Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner and the time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.60,000/- towards pain and suffering.
20. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced 6 Medical Bills and final bill for Rs. 1,18,590/- at Ex.P10.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.1,18,590/-.
21.
It is stated that petitioner was aged about 38 years and he was doing Labour work and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But PW.1 has not produced document to prove his income.

Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
22.
The petitioner has sustained two grievous injuries and taken treatment for 3 days as an inpatient in People Tree Hospitals, Bangalore.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of two months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.16,500/-
p.m for two months.

Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.33,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period.
23.
From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at People Tree Hospitals.
For 3 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.

Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.20,000/-
taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.

Gangadhara C M vs Manjunatha on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158902405/
5 24.
So far as future medical expense is concerned, even though PW.2 has deposed that petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants, but he has not given any estimation
. Hence, this court awards compensation under the head future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.30,000/-.

Thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl.
No Heads

Amount Rs.
1.
Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 60,000/-

2. Medical expenses Rs.1,18,590/-
3. Towards loss of income during Rs.33,000/-
 laid up period 4.

Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 20,000/-
 charges and nourishing food 5.

Future medical expenses Rs. 30,000/-
6. Loss of amenities and discomfort Rs.1,25,000/-

Therefore, this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,86,590/- (Rupees Three Lakh Eight Six Thousand Five Hundred Ninety only).
25.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered.
26. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.3,86,590/- + cost of Rs.2,000/- imposed vide order on IA No.IV and V.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.3,88,590/- (Rupees Three Lakh Eighty Eight Thousand Five Hundred Ninety only).
A Sum of Rs.3,56,590/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and Gangadhara C M vs Manjunatha on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158902405/
6 remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner through E- payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 3rd day of January 2026.)
(ROOPASHRI) XXII Addl. SCJ & ACJM Bengaluru.
